posts.caption: What if we stopped asking what a three-year-old should be able to do, and started noticing what they are already trying to understand?

At Beru, we deeply value the love and wisdom that grandparents bring to our children’s lives. 

We were delighted to celebrate Grandparents’ Day with our Beruvian grandparents, exploring their grandchild’s school, joining in the fun, sharing little moments, and making memories together.

What makes you, you?

Sometimes, understanding ourselves begins by listening to someone else.

As part of our big idea :All About Me, children turned to their friends with a simple invitation: What makes you special? What makes you, you?

Their answers became little glimpses into how children see themselves and how they begin to see one another.

Because every child has a story worth listening to.

How many Onam words do you know? 👀
Come discover them with us.

Pookalam 🌸
A flower carpet made with colours, patterns and petals.
We explored how flowers can come together to create something beautiful.

Sadhya 🍃
A traditional Onam feast served on a banana leaf.
We discovered the joy of sharing food and eating together.

Vadam Vali 🪢
Vadam means rope and vali means pull.
Our Beruvians discovered the meaning of the words through a little tug-of-war!

Pull, hold, balance, try again!
Through play, the word vali became something we could experience.

Pulikali 🐯
A traditional folk dance from Kerala, known for its playful tiger-like movements.
Our bodies became part of the story as we explored movement and expression.

Thiruvathirakali 🌿
A traditional Kerala dance performed in a circle.
We found rhythm, movement and togetherness as we moved with one another.

Vallam Kali 🚣🏽
Vallam means boat and Kali means play.
A traditional boat race that brings people together through rhythm, teamwork and celebration.

We all want to raise confident children.

But sometimes, in our effort to love, protect and help, we may unknowingly get in the way of their growing independence.

A gentle reminder to pause, reflect, and make space for children to try, struggle, and find their own way.

Because confidence grows when we let them.

“It’s been raining since we came to school!”
“It’s so dark and gloomy today!”

And yet, the monsoon brought us something to wonder about. 🌧️

Our Beruvians hands reached out to feel the rain, noticing its rhythm, its touch, and the world it changed around us.

Sometimes, the most meaningful experiences begin when you pause.

A few words from the families

Here’s what parents had to say about The Hundred Languages: A Sensory Play Date.

Our very first Playdate, and what a beautiful beginning it was.

At The Hundred Languages: A Sensory Play Date, children and families explored, discovered, created, and connected through experiences that invited them to see, touch, smell, hear, and taste the world in new ways.

From nature inspired provocations to collaborative sensory explorations, every interaction reminded us of something we deeply believe at Beru: children make meaning through relationships, curiosity, and hands-on experiences.

Thank you to all the families who joined us and made our first Playdate so special. We loved learning alongside you. 

Here’s to many more moments of wonder, connection, and discovery together.
